draft.emotion: positive and approving, simple and direct
notes: An irregular i-adjective. Only the plain present form is いい; all other forms use the stem よ- from よい (よかった, よくない, よくて).

senses.definition: Of high quality; pleasant, favourable, or desirable.

examples.emotion: cheerful and appreciative, opening a friendly conversation

senses.definition: Acceptable, suitable, or permitted (often after 〜ても).

examples.text: ここに座ってもいいですか。
examples.translation: Is it okay if I sit here?

senses.definition: Sufficient; not needing or wanting any more.

examples.translation: I don't need any more water, thank you.

draftBefore.emotion: positive and approving, simple and direct
notes: いい (ii) and よい (yoi) mean the same thing and are often interchangeable, though いい is more common in everyday spoken Japanese.
Note that when conjugating いい, you must use the stem よい (e.g., past tense is よかった).
